---
title: "convert-to-uploadable-mp4"
description: "Transcode any video to a widely-compatible H.264/AAC MP4 with fast-start"
---

## Overview

`convert-to-uploadable-mp4` transcodes a video into a **widely-compatible, upload-ready MP4**
using `ffmpeg`. It enforces:

- **H.264** video (`libx264`) with `yuv420p` chroma subsampling
- A baseline-friendly profile/level for broad device support
- **AAC** audio
- `+faststart` so the `moov` atom sits at the front of the file, enabling
  progressive download and instant playback while uploading.

```bash
convert_to_uploadable_mp4 input.mov
convert_to_uploadable_mp4 -c 20 -o out.mp4 input.mkv
```

## Dependencies

- `ffmpeg` on `PATH`

## Options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-c <num>` | H.264 CRF quality, 0–51 (lower = better / larger; default: `18`) |
| `-s <num>` | Downscale so the longer side is at most `<num>` px (preserves aspect ratio) |
| `-o <path>` | Output path (default: `<INPUT_STEM>_uploadable.mp4`) |
| `-y` | Overwrite the output file if it already exists |
| `-h` | Show help and exit. |

## Usage

```bash
# Basic — convert input.mov
convert_to_uploadable_mp4 input.mov

# Set quality and output path
convert_to_uploadable_mp4 -c 20 -o out.mp4 input.mkv

# Downscale to 1080p max and force overwrite
convert_to_uploadable_mp4 -s 1080 -y -o small.mp4 input.mp4
```

## Notes

- The output is guaranteed to have even dimensions (required by `yuv420p`).
- Without `-y`, the script exits with an error if the output file already exists.
- CRF 18 is visually lossless for most content; higher values trade quality for
  smaller files.
